nodes.rationale: Footer: reFLOP 0.1.11 | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 | No native baseline for this run.

nodes.label: cgroup v2 limits
nodes.rationale: Used only for safety rails; never RLIMIT_AS because CUDA reserves large virtual ranges.

nodes.label: seccomp-BPF
nodes.rationale: Primary mechanism for blocking execve, process creation, non-Unix sockets, ptrace and mount; works on all supported kernels without root.

nodes.label: ADR-004: Sandbox implementation
nodes.rationale: Landlock before exec covers every thread on every ABI (pre-ABI-8 Landlock restricts only the calling thread); seccomp after warm-up with TSYNC; data passed as fds; all new sockets denied.

nodes.label: ADR-016: cgroups only in reflopd-owned units
nodes.norm_label: adr-016: cgroups only in reflopd-owned units
nodes.rationale: A shell's own scope holds other processes; enabling controllers there fails and would affect the terminal.

nodes.label: ADR-031: Isolation probes run in CI and fail closed
nodes.norm_label: adr-031: isolation probes run in ci and fail closed
nodes.rationale: A skipping job would go green after a runner kernel change; strict mode fails instead of skipping and runs with user namespaces off and on.

nodes.label: ADR-035: Each worker gets its own memory limit below the shared one
nodes.norm_label: adr-035: each worker gets its own memory limit below the shared one
nodes.rationale: With only a shared memory.max the kernel killed the largest worker, not the grower; a 1/8-headroom margin makes the per-worker limit fail first.

nodes.label: I5: One sandboxed worker per identity-session
nodes.norm_label: i5: one sandboxed worker per identity-session

nodes.label: Pause Request Queue Limits
nodes.rationale: Caps held requests per session and in total so a Guest sending during a pause cannot grow reflopd until its cgroup OOM-kills it (#15).

nodes.label: Checkpoint Measurements (2026-11-18)
nodes.rationale: Side-stream ring checkpoints cost noise-level step time but hold an extra copy of state in GPU memory; synchronous writes were +83%.

nodes.label: Issue #2: session state lost with worker
nodes.norm_label: issue #2: session state lost with worker

nodes.label: ADR-028: Snapshots written durably and restored all or nothing
nodes.norm_label: adr-028: snapshots written durably and restored all or nothing
nodes.rationale: Two-phase write (SnapshotCut/SnapshotGo) reserves exact size against disk rail and quota; restore validates everything before committing all handles.

nodes.label: ADR-029: Guest checkpoints: Owner opt-in, 5-minute floor, no redo log
nodes.norm_label: adr-029: guest checkpoints: owner opt-in, 5-minute floor, no redo log
nodes.rationale: Real cost of checkpoints is disk writes (72 GiB/hour worst case), so Owner opt-in with a hard floor; redo log deferred until deterministic numerics are strict.

nodes.label: ADR-030: pause --now suspends GPU workers
nodes.rationale: CUDA driver checkpoint API frees the GPU in under a second without ending sessions; helper accepts only reflop workers since it can freeze processes.

nodes.label: Asynchronous Checkpoints
nodes.rationale: Server tensors are immutable, so holding references gives a consistent point-in-time cut without blocking execution.

nodes.label: Checkpoint as a Barrier
nodes.rationale: Without a barrier an upload could reach the worker before an earlier checkpoint and fail with HANDLE_EXISTS on replay.

nodes.label: Client Redo Log (deferred)
nodes.rationale: Replays inputs since the last checkpoint; bit-identical only with strict deterministic numerics, and needs a reconnect state machine.

nodes.label: Recoverable vs Final Session Loss
nodes.rationale: The client must never bring back a session the Owner ended on purpose.

nodes.label: Pinned Staging Ring (2 x 64 MiB)
nodes.rationale: Pinned memory cannot be swapped out, so it stays small to protect the Owner's desktop.

nodes.label: Fully Replicated State (rejected)
nodes.rationale: A standby worker doubles memory and compute and covers only crashes; streaming to client breaks the few-KB-per-step target; keeping state in reflopd puts Guest data in the daemon.

nodes.label: Network Exposure and Binding
nodes.rationale: Tailscale/WireGuard binding recommended; authentication required on every bind; TLS 1.3.

nodes.label: Owner Controls (pause, resume, kill, say)
nodes.rationale: Events shown to Guests are informational only.

nodes.label: reflopd invite (one-time invite code)
nodes.rationale: A failed attempt also consumes the invite so a leaked code cannot be brute-forced.

nodes.label: Pinned Runtimes (cu132, cu126, cpu)

nodes.norm_label: adr-018: reflopd sandboxes itself by re-exec

nodes.norm_label: adr-021: the client on pypi, uploaded from the signed release

nodes.norm_label: adr-023: a full gpu at startup is served once a probe succeeds

nodes.label: ADR-025: Unpairing on both sides
nodes.rationale: Guest half (Unpair message revokes own identity only) and Owner half (reflopd unpair = revoke + users delete), either order.

nodes.label: ADR-027: reflop run keeps OpenMP on one thread on macOS
nodes.norm_label: adr-027: reflop run keeps openmp on one thread on macos
nodes.rationale: Two OpenMP runtimes in one process fight once both start pools; KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK is unsafe; changing threading at import is surprising.
